flagsToAdd: Volume conservation alone gives necessary conditions, not a packing proof. For this choice task, eliminating the other listed answers and constructing the 20-piece subdivision suffices.
records.reason: Smaller cubes have integer edge 1 or 2, and both sizes occur. With v edge-2 cubes and u unit cubes, u+8v=27 and N=27-7v; only 20 among the listed options has this form. It is attained by one corner edge-2 cube and nineteen unit grid cubes. There is also an orientation-independent uniqueness check: each edge-2 cube contains a unit-radius ball. In an edge-3 container, every such ball center lies in [1,2]^3, so two centers would be at distance at most sqrt(3)<2 and their balls would overlap. Thus v=1 necessarily and N=20, E, even without relying on choice elimination. Volume conservation alone does not prove arbitrary formal packings; this supplemental geometry resolves that qualification. Retain the original volume/integer targets without inferring mastery of this advanced supplemental proof.
